title: Entropy-Based Diagnosis of Sampling Bias in Archaeological Predictive Modeling
description:
Code and derived data for an information-theoretic diagnostic of coverage imbalance in archaeological predictive modelling. Computes the Shannon entropy of the distribution of recorded sites across a partition of covariate space, derives observation weights in closed form as the normalised surprisal, and tests whether applying them changes the predictions of four frameworks (Random Forest, penalised-spline logistic GAM, MaxEnt in penalised-logistic form, and non-spatial Bayesian logistic regression) under both random and catchment-blocked cross-validation.

The input dataset is the published supplementary data of Yaworsky et al. (2020) for the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument, archived at tDAR (doi:10.6067/XCV8457626). It contains no coordinates: archaeological site locations in the United States are withheld under statutory protection. All entropy quantities are therefore defined over covariate space rather than geographic space.
